no_enrichment_test_reason: Anthocyanin pathway nodes and heat studies are not an exchangeable random universe; heat commonly affects multiple linked pathway nodes, so a post hoc hypergeometric p-value would overstate evidence.

direct_heat_white_plasticity_example.result: elevated-temperature summer flowers are white; anthocyanins occur in spring flowers while summer flowers accumulate UV-absorbing flavonoids/phenolics

working_model: Genetic/regulatory perturbations and thermal repression can independently reduce or reroute flux through overlapping pigment-network nodes and converge on pale/achromatic floral phenotypes.
why_bio5_nonreplication_is_not_a_contrad: Published heat responses are conditional on genotype, developmental stage and light environment; therefore heat can be a real molecular perturbation without generating a universal cross-species BIO5 main effect.
next_decisive_test: natural colour genotype/morph x temperature common-garden experiment with pigment chemistry and targeted pathway expression; primary estimand is genotype/morph-by-temperature interaction
hard_nonclaims: does not rescue the failed legacy BIO5 replication
does not prove heat generated the global H2 white/nonwhite geometry
does not establish a universal anthocyanin mechanism across betalain or carotenoid systems
does not establish nonwhite-to-white evolutionary transition asymmetry
